migration.rationale: Live data already has a single de facto owner (dominant source_ref-hash scheme, with the only competing live cohort fully alias-covered). No live migration is required to reach single ownership of the DATA. What remains open is a lifecycle-contract decision (should packet_key survive rename / become revision-qualified / converge on stableFileId), which is a design question, not a migration -- and per the pasted task instructions this report performs design analysis only where migration IS required; since migration is not required, no migration design is produced.

resultRationale: Live packet_key ownership is empirically single (99.9% of atlas_packets rows resolve to one formula-family, with the resolver actively rejecting both non-live candidate schemes) -- so this is NOT an active OWNER_CONFLICT at the data layer, and NOT a MIGRATION_REQUIRED or COMPATIBILITY_LAYER_REQUIRED case (the one compatibility layer needed, the alias table, already exists and is fully applied). The genuine open gap is that no written contract states what packet_key is supposed to mean over a file's lifecycle -- specifically whether it must survive rename, whether it should be revision-qualified, or whether it should ultimately be derived from stableFileId (the already-frozen UUIDv7 file-lifecycle identity) rather than from source_ref directly. That undefined contract is exactly what blocks deciding whether packet-key-builder.ts's hex64/node-scoped candidate is the right future owner, the wrong one, or irrelevant. Distinct from and independent of both open operator decisions (S01-08K apply token; PACKET-WRITER-PRODUCTION-OWNER-01 caller choice).
